Account Manager pour Academic Work
A propos du rôle
Don't leave fit to chance ! Chez Academic Work, nous sommes les experts du recrutement des professionnels en début de carrière, avec une ambition claire : devenir LE leader de la prédiction de performance.
Depuis près de 30 ans, nous déployons notre expertise dans 6 pays. Nous continuons notre croissance, et c'est pourquoi nous recherchons deux Account Managers pour renforcer notre équipe genevoise.
Notre bureau de Genève est composé de 25 collaborateurs animés par une culture de l'ambition et de plus de 150 consultants que nous sommes fiers d'accompagner chaque mois. Ce qui nous distingue ? Une culture d'entreprise forte, un engagement sans faille de nos collaborateurs, et une satisfaction client qui nous motive chaque jour à aller plus loin.
Alors, prêt(e) à faire la différence ?
Tâches
Le rôle d'Account Manager est un savant mélange de détermination et de réflexion stratégique. Tu portes en permanence deux casquettes : celle du Hunter, moteur de notre expansion, et celle du Conseiller, partenaire de confiance des chefs d'entreprise. Ton talent ? Savoir ouvrir des portes là où les autres voient des obstacles, puis adapter notre expertise aux réalités du marché et des talents disponibles pour créer une solution unique.

s.h: Concrètement, tu pilotes ton activité autour de quatre axes
s.t:
Prospection et développement de portefeuille : C'est le cœur de ta mission. Tu construis et gères ton propre portefeuille de clients de A à Z. Le cold calling est ton levier quotidien pour convaincre et obtenir des rendez\-vous stratégiques avec des responsables d'entreprise.
Analyse de besoin et négociation : Tu rencontres des directeurs et managers pour analyser leurs besoins. Tu établis les profils de candidats recherchés et mènes les négociations tarifaires. Ton but est de convaincre tes interlocuteurs de la valeur de notre accompagnement pour bâtir des collaborations à long terme.
Expertise marché et synergie interne : Fort de ta connaissance du terrain, tu apportes un regard éclairé à tes clients. Une fois le besoin identifié, tu travailles en lien étroit avec nos recruteurs.
Rigueur et résultats : Tu es responsable de tes performances. Pour assurer des résultats constants, tu appliques nos méthodes de travail avec précision, du premier contact jusqu'à la conclusion de l'accord (le closing).
Nous cherchons un tempérament, pas un CV
Peu importe tes études ou ton passé professionnel, nous cherchons les traits de caractère suivants :
Le sens de la conviction : Tu n'hésites pas à donner ton avis, même face à une figure d'autorité. Tu préfères une discussion franche au consensus facile.
Une résilience sans faille : L'échec te pousse à redoubler d'efforts. Un "non" n'est jamais une fin en soi, mais le point de départ pour trouver une autre solution.
Le goût de l'accomplissement : Tu as besoin de te fixer des défis pour avancer. Tu aimes la compétition et tu cherches un environnement où tes efforts sont récompensés à leur juste valeur.
Une curiosité naturelle : Tu aimes creuser un sujet pour en comprendre les racines. Tu poses les bonnes questions pour comprendre un problème avant d'agir.
Le sens de l'autonomie : Tu apprécies la liberté d'organiser tes journées et tu sais faire preuve d'une grande rigueur personnelle pour atteindre tes objectifs.
Prérequis
0 à 3 ans d'expérience après la fin de tes études.
Pas besoin d'expérience en Sales : nous te formons de A à Z via notre AW Sales Academy.
Français parfait et niveau avancé en anglais (C1\).
Permis de conduire (catégorie B).
Ce que nous t'offrons
Un écosystème de high\-performers : Un environnement exigeant et stimulant où l'on se tire vers le haut et où les succès sont célébrés ensemble (voyages, kick\-offs).
L'impact comme véritable moteur : Tu auras un impact direct sur le business de tes clients et sur la trajectoire des jeunes talents.
Think big \& make it happen : Un salaire fixe évolutif et un système de commissions totalement déplafonné. Ici, ton ambition est la seule limite.
L'AW Sales Academy : Un programme d'élite (3 semaines d'onboarding \+ coaching continu) pour transformer ton potentiel en expertise B2B.
Une autonomie stratégique : Une grande liberté pour gérer ton agenda et piloter ton portefeuille de clients.

About WorkWhile
WorkWhile is on a mission to help workers earn a better living and live better lives. 83 million Americans work hourly jobs: the true backbone of the hospitality, catering, and event industries. These workers often face highly volatile schedules, sudden booking surges, minimum wage pay, and limited benefits, leading to financial instability.
WorkWhile identifies the best, most reliable hourly workers and matches them with shifts that fit their skills, location, and life.

For high-volume catering companies, stadium and venue operators, corporate food service providers, and large-scale event producers, we provide instant access to a vetted, high-quality workforce to seamlessly scale up for major events and peak periods.

For workers, we provide stable income and unmatched benefits, including next-day pay, free telehealth services, upskilling, and financial wellness tools.
We have the audacious goal to align incentives and solve inefficiencies in the labor market, disrupting the $650 billion staffing and recruiting market. Backed by Khosla Ventures and recognized by the Inc. 5000 for 10x growth, WorkWhile is reshaping the future of work in hospitality and live events.

WorkWhile is looking for an Enterprise Account Manager - Hospitality to join our team and build long-term, trusting relationships with our enterprise hospitality and event clients.

This role is focused on managing a portfolio of high-volume accounts, including catering conglomerates, national contract food service providers, sports and entertainment venue operators, and premier event management groups, ensuring they have the right workforce to keep operations running smoothly, especially during peak seasons, major event rollouts, and sudden booking surges.
You will serve as the primary point of contact for hospitality enterprise accounts, driving satisfaction, retention, and growth while acting as a strategic partner who understands the fast-paced, high-stakes nature of food service, catering, and venue management.

Lead Account Relationship: Serve as the lead point of contact for all account management matters for enterprise hospitality and event clients, including staffing planning, shift fulfillment, and ongoing labor strategy.
Build Executive & Regional Alignment: Build and maintain strong, long-lasting relationships with regional event/culinary directors, general managers, corporate food service directors, venue concessionaires, and VP-level operations leaders.
Understand Industry Dynamics: Develop a deep understanding of each client’s operational environment, including hyper-seasonal staffing volatility, last-minute event bookings/cancellations, variable labor costs, and guest service standards, to proactively meet their workforce needs.
Drive Contract Growth & Retention: Maintain and grow client accounts, identifying upsell and expansion opportunities across regional event sites, venue networks, multi-unit properties, or new culinary/hospitality labor categories.
Act as a Trusted Advisor: Develop trusted advisor relationships with key hospitality accounts, aligning WorkWhile's workforce solutions to their operational goals, ROI targets, and guest experience standards.
Ensure Operational Excellence: Ensure timely and successful fulfillment of shifts in line with strict client SLAs, worker reliability metrics, and service quality expectations for high-profile events.
Transparent Stakeholder Communication: Communicate the progress of weekly, monthly, and quarterly workforce initiatives clearly to both internal operations teams and enterprise client executives.
Track & Forecast Metrics: Forecast and track key account metrics including fill rates, worker attendance/performance, client satisfaction scores, and revenue retention and expansion.
Deliver Business Reviews: Prepare regular account health reports and quarterly business reviews tailored to venue operators, contract food service executives, and catering leadership teams.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with the Sales team to expand WorkWhile's presence across new venue networks or regional operator groups, and collaborate with internal Operations teams to ensure fulfillment during peak periods (e.g., stadium game days, peak catering seasons, major conferences).
Issue Escalation & Resolution: Assist with challenging client requests or live-event operational escalations, providing quick and effective resolutions to minimize disruption to the guest experience.

Experience: 3+ years experience as an Account Manager, ideally within the contract food service, event management, catering, venue operations, or flexible workforce solutions industries.
Deep Hospitality & Event IQ: A profound understanding of the logistics behind large-scale catering, stadium operations, corporate dining, and how workforce reliability directly impacts guest experience and margin.
Executive Presence & Influence: Demonstrated ability to communicate, present, and influence stakeholders at all levels, from regional culinary directors and venue GMs to VP-level hospitality executives.
Multi-Unit Expertise: Experience managing multi-unit, enterprise-scale hospitality accounts, venue networks, or multi-city event portfolios.
Tech Stack Proficiency: Solid experience with CRM software (Salesforce or similar) and Google Suite.
Track Record of Growth: Proven track record of delivering client-focused labor solutions, maintaining high customer retention rates, and hitting revenue growth/expansion targets.
Agility & Attention to Detail: Ability to juggle multiple complex enterprise accounts and fast-moving event timelines while maintaining sharp attention to detail.
Communication Skills: Excellent listening, negotiation, presentation, verbal, and written communication skills.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. At Wolt, we create technology that brings local communities, merchants and customers closer together. What started with restaurant delivery has grown into a broader local commerce platform, helping customers discover and access more of what their cities have to offer.
As our Retail business continues to grow, we're looking for a Senior Sales Regional Enterprise Manager to expand our selection of high-value regional retail partners. You'll join our Enterprise Sales team and take ownership of some of the most important regional acquisition opportunities across priority retail verticals, helping shape what customers can find on Wolt in their cities. This role can be based in Berlin, Cologne or Frankfurt.
What you'll be doing

You'll combine strong commercial execution with a strategic view on which partners can have the greatest impact on Wolt's selection, coverage and long-term growth.

Own the end-to-end sales cycle for regional Enterprise retail opportunities, from prospecting and qualification through negotiation, contracting and signing.
Build and manage a high-quality pipeline of larger regional retailers and multi-location partners across priority verticals such as grocery, convenience, pet, pharmacy and beauty.
Develop a deep understanding of prospective partners' businesses and create compelling commercial propositions that demonstrate the value of partnering with Wolt.
Lead complex commercial negotiations, balancing partner needs with sustainable economics and Wolt's long-term business objectives.
Build strong relationships with senior decision-makers and act as a trusted commercial partner throughout the sales process.
Work closely with internal teams including Operations, Account Management, Finance, Legal, Marketing and Product to structure partnerships and enable successful launches.
Take ownership beyond the signature, ensuring a strong handover and initial rollout so that newly acquired partners can successfully go live and scale.
Use market insights, pipeline data and commercial learnings to identify opportunities, prioritize the highest-impact accounts and continuously improve our regional Enterprise sales approach.
Contribute to sharing best practices and raising the bar for Enterprise sales execution across the wider team.

About Mixpanel
Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at .

Our Select Accounts team owns Mixpanel 's most strategic accounts. We're a small group of experienced enterprise sellers who run the full motion: protect the base, expand within it, and open net new logos from a defined target list. We don't split farmers and hunters here — everyone does both, and everyone is measured the same way: deep account relationships, disciplined pipeline, and quarter-over-quarter growth in their book.

You'll own Mixpanel 's most complex and highest-value accounts — a mix of existing enterprise customers and net new target logos — running renewal, expansion, and new logo motions in parallel.

This is a role for someone who has done this before at scale: you solve ambiguous, multi-year account problems by distilling them into a clear, scalable plan, and you set a standard for how the team approaches account strategy, forecasting, and executive engagement.

You'll mentor other Account Executives on deal strategy and multi-threading, and your account plans and playbooks will shape how the broader team operates.

In your first 90 days, you'll build a territory plan covering your full account list, map the key relationships and growth opportunities in each account, and present your go-forward strategy to leadership.

Build and execute account plans that connect Mixpanel 's capabilities to each customer's business priorities, anticipating multi-year account trajectory
Develop multi-threaded relationships from the practitioner level through the C-suite, creating durable champions at every layer
Run regular business reviews that show what's working and surface the next growth opportunity
Forecast accurately and keep pipeline clean in Salesforce — no sandbags, no surprises
Identify and close expansion opportunities within your book — new teams, new products, upgraded tiers
Prospect and close net new logos from your named target list alongside your existing account motion
Run a disciplined sales process using MEDDPICC; qualify hard and close on time
Partner with Solutions Engineers on product demonstrations and proofs of concept that accelerate deals
Build pipeline across all four sourcing channels: self-generated outbound, BDR, channel partners, and inbound
Collaborate with Customer Success to make sure customers realize value after the sale
Bring customer and market signals back to Product — you're closest to the problem
Set the standard for team playbooks on account planning, forecasting, and executive engagement, and mentor other Account Executives on deal strategy

Our SMB and Commercial teams sit at the core of Miro 's new business engine. SMB AEs work with small and scaling businesses — companies between 1 and 500 employees — in a fast-paced, high-volume environment where momentum matters. Commercial AEs work with mid-market companies from 500 to 3,000 employees — large enough to demand a real evaluation process, agile enough that the right champion can move a deal in weeks.
Together, these teams represent the full spectrum from high-velocity transactional selling to increasingly rigorous, multi-stakeholder deals. If you're a strong SMB closer looking to level up, or a mid-market seller who thrives on volume and strategy in equal measure, this is where you belong.

Both roles own the full sales cycle — from first conversation to closed deal — across a mix of inbound leads, outbound prospecting, and existing account expansion. The core motion is the same: generate pipeline, run disciplined discovery, connect Miro 's platform to business outcomes, and close. The segment and deal complexity differ, but the fundamentals are shared.
SMB AEs manage a high-volume book of 1–500 EE prospects with fast cycles and direct decision-makers. Commercial AEs balance a similar volume with deeper, multi-stakeholder deals requiring formal business cases and director-to-C-suite engagement.

Own the full sales cycle Prospecting and discovery through to demo, negotiation, and close across your territory — high-volume for SMB, a blend of volume and depth for Commercial.
Drive net-new logo acquisition Develop and execute a territory strategy to land new accounts in your segment, owning every stage from outbound prospecting to signed contract.
Generate and maintain pipeline Strike the right balance between managing inbound leads and generating outbound pipeline. Keep a healthy, well-forecasted pipeline at all times.
Run value-first discovery Apply MEDDPICC and Command of the Message to uncover genuine pain, connect Miro 's platform to business outcomes, and build a clear case for change.
Execute a hybrid motion Pursue net-new logos while identifying expansion signals within existing accounts. Understand when to go wide and when to go deep.
Engage decision-makers at the right level
SMB: Work directly with founders, ops leads, and team managers to identify pain and close quickly.
Commercial: Adapt your style from LOB champion to VP/C-suite in the same deal cycle. Build relationships with economic buyers and communicate Miro 's value in terms of business outcomes.
Forecast with accuracy Maintain CRM hygiene in Salesforce, manage your pipeline with discipline, and commit to numbers you can stand behind.
Collaborate across your POD Work in lockstep with Renewals, Customer Success, Marketing, and — for Commercial — Solution Engineering and Value Advisory, to ensure a joined-up customer experience at every stage.
What you’ll need

s.h: For both SMB and Commercial AE
s.t:
Working knowledge of MEDDPICC and Command of the Message, applied consistently with a drive to sharpen both.
A high-velocity mindset — comfortable running many deals simultaneously with the discipline to prioritise and focus.
Strong prioritisation and adaptability — able to balance inbound demand, outbound prospecting, and expansion opportunities effectively.
Resilience and coachability — you treat lost deals as learning and apply feedback fast.
Proficiency with Salesforce for pipeline management, plus Outreach (or similar) and Gong.
AI fluency and curiosity — comfortable leveraging AI tools to improve prospect research, outreach preparation, account planning, and productivity.
For SMB AE: 1–4 years in a SaaS or B2B tech sales environment, including at least some full-cycle closing experience or a strong SDR background.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

As Partner Account Manager DACH you will help manage and execute the partnerships that accelerate Claude adoption, unlock new capabilities and drive outcomes for our joint customers across Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
You will own a defined set of named partners end to end — a mix of (a) in-country DACH practices of our global system integrators (e.g.

Accenture, Deloitte, Capgemini, PwC, BCG), where you work hand in hand with the GSI alliance owners who hold the global relationships, and (b) regional system integrators, consultancies and AI-native boutiques that DACH enterprises and the Mittelstand actually buy from.

The DACH partner book is split between you and the Head of Partnerships DACH and CEE; for every partner assigned to you, you own the plan, the enablement path, the co-sell motion with our DACH sales team and the partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline that results from it.

This is a builder role: partner-sourced pipeline in DACH is still a small fraction of our open pipeline, and there is a first playbook but no established machine. We need someone who has taken partnerships from zero to a repeatable revenue engine in this market before, not someone who has inherited and administered an existing partner book.

Run each partner as a structured pursuit: stakeholder map (country lead, AI/data practice lead, alliance lead, key account partners), joint account plan, agreed target accounts and a quarterly cadence.
For your assigned GSI country practices: activate the DACH teams against the global frameworks and translate them into concrete joint accounts. For your assigned regional SIs / boutiques: build the relationship from scratch (selection, onboarding into the Claude Partner Network, enablement, first joint deals).
Guide partners in building repeatable Claude offerings (Claude Code / agentic engineering rollouts, agentic use cases, enterprise adoption programs) for the priority DACH industries: automotive and manufacturing, financial services and insurance, public sector, telco, pharma and chemicals.
Drive co-selling with the DACH AEs, Applied AI and Technical Success teams: introduce partners into the right accounts, bring partner-sourced opportunities to sales, and make sure every partner-attached deal is tagged correctly in Salesforce.

Own and drive the KPIs for your portfolio: Partner delivered use-cases, partner-sourced pipeline, partner-influenced pipeline and revenue, consultants enabled and certified, partners progressing through CPN tiers, joint proposals submitted.
Establish clear success metrics with each partner and drive regular business reviews against targets
Report on partnership health, progress, and commercial outcomes with data-driven insights
Every deal that runs through your partners must be set up for customer success and expansion: agree success criteria for joint accounts, make sure the partner delivers implementation and adoption support, and feed what you learn back into our partner program and the DACH sales team.
Market development and brand building
Represent Anthropic in the DACH partner ecosystem — partner events, joint customer events, and partner-led marketing in German.
Adapt the global partner playbook to DACH buying behaviour (Mittelstand vs. DAX/SMI enterprises, long procurement cycles, works councils, preference for local delivery partners) and decide deliberately what not to copy.
Navigate the regulatory and sovereignty topics that come up in almost every DACH deal (GDPR, EU AI Act, data residency, regulated industries such as banking and insurance) together with the partner and our internal experts.
Build differentiated joint value propositions with partners so that Claude is the default recommendation of the DACH consulting ecosystem.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. Team Leadership & Coaching

Pipeline Building: Maintain a live talent bench by proactively building relationships with potential FSA candidates in your states, ensuring the region is never understaffed.
Workforce Planning: Partner with the Operations team to forecast FSA headcount needs based on regional acquisition targets and attrition trends.
Recruitment Reporting: Track time-to-fill and onboarding completion rates, flagging recruitment blockers to leadership in a timely manner.
Sales Operations & Performance
Drive Targets: Own region-level acquisition targets (weekly and monthly) and ensure individual FSAs meet their assigned quotas.
Track Activity: Monitor daily field activity metrics, visits completed, leads generated, acquisitions recorded, and follow-ups made, and intervene when performance trends downward.
Field Support: Join FSAs in the field to support complex or at-risk acquisition opportunities where direct engagement is needed.
Pipeline Management: Maintain clean, accurate, and up-to-date CRM records across your team on a daily basis.
Process & Quality Assurance
Process Adherence: Ensure all field activity is executed in line with the business's acquisition playbook and within agreed timelines.
Quality Control: Review and score FSA fieldwork quality; share structured feedback in weekly team review sessions.
Handoff Management: Coordinate a seamless handoff from FSAs to Implementation and Data Entry teams following a successful acquisition.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Relay structured feedback on lead quality, market conditions, and field blockers to the Growth and Marketing teams.
Leadership Reporting: Provide leadership with clear weekly reports on team field activity, acquisition rates, recruitment status, and immediate blockers.
Experience & Background
4–5 years of total experience in field sales, B2B sales, or territory management.
At least 1–2 years of experience in a team lead, coordinator, or supervisory capacity.
Demonstrated experience recruiting or building commission-based sales teams, either formally or as part of a team lead role.
Proven track record of consistently meeting or exceeding acquisition or sales quotas.
Experience coaching and developing junior field sales reps on activity execution and objection handling.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical field sales experience preferred.
Skills & Competencies
Natural Team Builder: Proven ability to find the right people, bring them in, and get them performing fast.
Frontline Leader: Ready to lead from the front with no hesitation going into the field alongside FSAs to model what great acquisition looks like.
Balanced Management Style: Ability to balance accountability with empathy, holding people to numbers to genuinely drive their professional growth.
Data-Informed & People-First: Skillful use of daily activity metrics to coach rather than micromanage.
Agility & Focus: Highly adaptable to fast-paced, high-growth environments with the ability to manage competing regional priorities seamlessly.
Radical Ownership: Deep commitment to regional outcomes, celebrating wins together, and treating misses as learning opportunities.
Communication & Tools: Strong verbal and written communication skills to deliver structured feedback, run effective team meetings, and represent the region to leadership. Comfort with sales work tools and daily pipeline management workflows.
What success looks like in this role
Weeks 1–2: Complete full product and playbook onboarding. Shadow all FSAs in the field. Establish cadences with team members. Audit the existing FSA recruitment pipeline and playbook.
Weeks 3–4: Run first structured field review sessions. Identify any headcount gaps and initiate active FSA recruitment in understaffed states.
Month 2: Fully own regional KPI tracking on a weekly basis. Fill open FSA roles and ensure all new hires are progressing through onboarding on schedule.
Month 3: Region achieves 85%–100% of the monthly acquisition quota. FSAs have active coaching plans in place, and the recruitment pipeline remains healthy.
